items.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: There’s a bass player on one of Benny Waters’ CDs, Bob Bowman — no actually, I’m sorry, that’s Claude Williams’ CD, Bob Bowman.

ctx.x: Well who has become your favorite bass players then?

Well I enjoy music from a lot of different bass players. I like some of Ray Brown, some of Ron Carter’s. There’s a bass player on one of Benny Waters’ CDs, Bob Bowman — no actually, I’m sorry, that’s Claude Williams’ CD, Bob Bowman. And I basically try to listen for specific recordings that I like. I don’t buy them just for the artist, but for that particular recording. Like for example I like Ron Carter on “Alone Together” with Jim Hall. So particular recordings, that’s what I look mostly for. And some of the…
Is there a gig or a particular series of gigs — it’s almost the same question — but that you felt like man this is the big time in the jazz world? When did that particularly happen?
